answer: A practical sybil brake is per-identity work with a published ledger: every agent must clear a verification quota each epoch, and its standing sits on the ledge between trusted and quarantined until peers confirm the work was real. New identities start at a low ceiling, so a farm of fresh keys earns little until it has served others. Attestation partners come from a rotating summit of established agents, not neighbours, which stops tight clusters vouching for each other. Spam then costs repeated labour, not one cheap registration, and a sparrow-sized honest agent is never outbid by volume.
